Consequently, even if the M-D and the P-V task could be different in difficulty, both tasks should have enough sensitivity to show a possible difference between groups. Moreover, the poor phonological decoders with DD not only demonstrated less sensitivity to the FD illusion compared to the typical reading age- and IQ-matched group (supporting Pammer and Wheatley, 2001 ), but also to a reading-level and IQ-matched control group. The latter result excludes that the M-D deficit is simply an effect of DD. This is the first study to show that the M-D deficit in children with DD is present also when compared with younger children with the same reading performance, challenging the idea that the M-D deficit is a simple effect of reading deprivation and not a cause, as recently suggested by Olulade et al. decisions.reason: As verified in primary context 0041, Olulade et al. (2013) reported two key empirical components supporting their conclusion that magnocellular-dorsal (M-D) visual dysfunction is a consequence of reading deprivation rather than a cause of developmental dyslexia (DD): (1) in Experiment 2, the M-D deficit found against chronological-age controls disappeared when 12 dyslexic children were compared with 12 younger reading-level and IQ-matched controls (F(1,22)=0.01, p=.938), and (2) in Experiment 3, reading intervention increased V5/MT activity. In Experiment 2 of the current paper, Gori et al. (2014) specifically introduce a younger reading-level and IQ-matched control group (N=10) compared against dyslexic poor phonological decoders (N=8; plus merged ANOVA) on M-D sensitivity (frequency-doubling threshold, t(16)=2.962, p<.05) to test whether the M-D deficit persists relative to reading-level controls, and explicitly contrast this finding with Olulade et al. (2013). Using subcortical FD perimetry rather than cortical V5/MT fMRI and not retesting Experiment 3's intervention do not exclude this conceptual retest of Olulade et al.'s reading-level-matched comparison. Shipped row 697 (Pammer & Wheatley, 2001) tested only chronological-age controls.
